question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR as the canonical node-hosted tool contract after the two public API compatibility blockers are fixed?
rationale: The PR changes which connected-node capabilities can become model-visible executable tools, so automation cannot choose the permanent trust, provenance, and compatibility boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Accept PR Path After API Repairs
options.body: Default or overload the Swift initializer, remove or implement the no-op client option, refresh the branch, then land if the trust model is accepted.

options.title: Pause On Canonical Design Issue
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/8287 as the design owner and pause this PR until the node-to-model contract is narrowed.

options.title: Reject Direct Node Tool Advertisement
options.body: Keep wrapper plugins or MCP integrations as the supported path and avoid a first-class connected-node tool surface for now.

recommendation.title: Accept PR Path After API Repairs
recommendation.body: Default or overload the Swift initializer, remove or implement the no-op client option, refresh the branch, then land if the trust model is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the current candidate PR and has the strongest current history across the Gateway, Swift, and plugin contract surfaces involved in this choice.
